evidence.limitation: These values are warning operating limits for a bounded synthetic disposable smoke and unchanged common runtime contracts. They are not production SLOs, capacity evidence or shared-environment generation acceptance. Stage-specific latency alerts are intentionally excluded because the pilot observed end-to-end paths rather than independently measured render, upload and metadata latency distributions.

DocumentServiceErrorRate.suppression: Fewer than 20 requests or only success/invalid_request outcomes.
DocumentServiceErrorRate.recovery: The five-minute unexpected-error ratio returns to 10% or lower.
DocumentServiceErrorRate.response: Split failures by transport and status, inspect safe logs/traces, then follow PostgreSQL and object-store lookup dependencies.

DocumentHighLatency.basis: unchanged Dashboard common request contract, supported by 1.104ms and 7.929ms Document lookup observations
DocumentHighLatency.recovery: The five-minute request p95 returns to 250ms or lower.
DocumentHighLatency.response: Split latency by transport and correlate PostgreSQL/object-store duration with a representative trace.

DocumentGenerationStageFailure.basis: Document-local low-volume partial-effect contract; one metadata failure left an object and recorded zero registrations
DocumentGenerationStageFailure.suppression: No render, upload or metadata operation ended in a bounded non-success outcome.
DocumentGenerationStageFailure.recovery: The last bounded generation-stage failure ages out of the five-minute window.
DocumentGenerationStageFailure.response: Identify the fixed render, upload or metadata stage, inspect its dependency and correlated trace, and preserve orphan-risk evidence before retry.

DocumentLookupFailure.basis: Document-local low-traffic result contract; the pilot independently observed a partial lookup
DocumentLookupFailure.suppression: All completed lookups are complete or empty without omitted documents or failures.
DocumentLookupFailure.recovery: The last partial or failed lookup ages out of the five-minute window.
DocumentLookupFailure.response: Separate metadata from object-store lookup, inspect omitted-document and dependency outcomes, and do not infer retrievability from registration alone.

DocumentEventFailure.basis: Document-local low-volume partial-effect contract; unlike Dashboard, a ten-event gate would hide one actionable failure
DocumentEventFailure.suppression: The worker is disabled or no malformed/error/cancelled registration completed in five minutes.
DocumentEventFailure.recovery: The last failed registration ages out of the five-minute window.
DocumentEventFailure.response: Inspect the bounded registration outcome, failing stage and Kafka readiness without exposing event values.

DocumentEventStalled.basis: unchanged Dashboard worker contract; 30s exceeds the fixed 8s render, 8s upload and 2s metadata timeout chain plus scheduling margin
DocumentEventStalled.suppression: Worker enabled is zero or in-flight age is zero.
DocumentEventStalled.recovery: Completion or cancellation resets in-flight age to zero.
DocumentEventStalled.response: Inspect render, upload, metadata and Kafka readiness with a correlated trace; preserve offset and orphan-risk evidence before restart.

DocumentEventWorkerFailed.suppression: The worker is disabled or its failed gauge is zero.
DocumentEventWorkerFailed.recovery: A successful completion clears the failed gauge while the worker remains enabled.
DocumentEventWorkerFailed.response: Inspect the last bounded worker outcome and stage diagnostics; distinguish failed from disabled and healthy idle.

DocumentEventCommitFailure.suppression: No registration offset commit failure occurred in five minutes.
DocumentEventCommitFailure.recovery: The last commit failure ages out of the five-minute window.
DocumentEventCommitFailure.response: Inspect bounded commit diagnostics and broker readiness, then preserve offset and document evidence before retry.

DocumentResourcePressure.basis: unchanged Dashboard common resource contract and identical 300m/256Mi limits
DocumentResourcePressure.suppression: Both CPU and memory remain at or below 80% of their deployment limits.
DocumentResourcePressure.recovery: Both resource signals remain below their thresholds.
DocumentResourcePressure.response: Inspect lookup/generation load, runtime memory, throttling, Pod events and rollout identity.

DocumentUnavailable.recovery: The Deployment returns to its desired available replica count.
DocumentUnavailable.response: Inspect rollout, readiness, configuration and read dependencies before rollback.

DocumentTelemetryMissing.suppression: The Deployment is unavailable or bounded Go runtime samples are present.
DocumentTelemetryMissing.recovery: A bounded Go runtime sample resumes.
DocumentTelemetryMissing.response: Verify OTLP configuration, Alloy receiver and remote-write health before changing the rule.

DocumentTelemetryDeliveryFailure.suppression: Delivery failure/drop counters do not increase; absent exporter series do not fabricate failure.
DocumentTelemetryDeliveryFailure.recovery: All five-minute failure/drop increases return to zero.
DocumentTelemetryDeliveryFailure.response: Identify the failed signal/backend and inspect bounded retry/drop counters while preserving service availability.

DocumentTelemetryBacklog.suppression: No samples are pending and exporter queue use is 80% or lower; absent series do not fabricate backlog.
DocumentTelemetryBacklog.recovery: Pending samples clear and exporter queues return to 80% or lower.
DocumentTelemetryBacklog.response: Check backend reachability and Alloy queue/WAL health, then verify recovery within two minutes.

DocumentUnexpectedRestart.suppression: No Go Document container restart occurred in 15 minutes.
DocumentUnexpectedRestart.recovery: The last restart ages out of the 15-minute window.
DocumentUnexpectedRestart.response: Inspect prior state, safe logs, Pod events, resource pressure and rollout identity.
